# Vendored libraries

`fg-bundle.min.js` is a single esbuild IIFE bundle exposing
`window.ForceGraph3D` (3d-force-graph 1.77.0, MIT), `window.ForceGraph`
(force-graph 1.51.4, MIT: the 2D canvas renderer), `window.SpriteText`
(three-spritetext 1.10.0, MIT) and `window.THREE` (three.js 0.185.0, MIT),
built over ONE shared copy of three.js so the sprite labels and the 3D scene
use the same version. It is inlined into every generated page, so the page is
fully self-contained: no CDN fetch, no blank page when a CDN is unreachable,
and nothing about your graph leaves your machine. Both renderers travel in the
one bundle because the page has a 3D/2D switch and must keep a single
`<script>` for the library.

Rebuild recipe (`package.json` and `package-lock.json` next to this file pin
every package in the bundle, transitive ones included, so the rebuild is
reproducible; bump a version there, run this, commit all three files):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fgbuild && cp package.json package-lock.json /tmp/fgbuild/ && cd /tmp/fgbuild
npm ci
printf 'import ForceGraph3D from "3d-force-graph";\nimport ForceGraph from "force-graph";\nimport SpriteText from "three-spritetext";\nimport * as THREE from "three";\nwindow.ForceGraph3D = ForceGraph3D;\nwindow.ForceGraph = ForceGraph;\nwindow.SpriteText = SpriteText;\nwindow.THREE = THREE;\n' > entry.js
npx esbuild entry.js --bundle --minify --format=iife --outfile=fg-bundle.min.js
cp fg-bundle.min.js <repo>/ttl3d/vendor/ && cd <repo>
python ttl3d/vendor/licenses.py /tmp/fgbuild ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md
```

The viewer needs all four globals; `tests/test_bundle.py` checks them, that the
pins are exact and locked, and that `LICENSES.md` names every runtime package
of the lockfile, so a rebuild that drops one fails the suite instead of
breaking pages silently.

Pinned upstream versions in the shipped bundle: 3d-force-graph 1.77.0,
force-graph 1.51.4, three-spritetext 1.10.0, three.js 0.185.0 (the bundle's
tail carries the three.js license banner); esbuild as pinned in
`package.json`. The bundle also inlines their dependencies (d3 modules,
kapsule, three-render-objects and others, all under permissive licences);
`LICENSES.md` next to this file lists every one with its licence and copyright
line, as those licences require, and is generated by `licenses.py`, never
edited by hand.
